title: Canonical right-derived comparison respects an exact adjoint square
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal A_0,\mathcal B_0$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Fix additive adjunctions $L:\mathcal B\rightleftarrows\mathcal A:R$ and $L_0:\mathcal B_0\rightleftarrows\mathcal A_0:R_0$, with $L,L_0$ exact. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A_0$ and $W:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B_0$ be exact additive functors. Fix natural isomorphisms $a:VL\cong L_0W$ and $c:WR\cong R_0V$ which respect adjuncts: for every $t:LM\to N$, the adjunct of $V(t)a_M^{-1}$ is $c_NW(t^\sharp)$. Suppose total right derived functors $RR,RR_0$ exist everywhere, with their canonical derived adjunctions [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. Write $D(V),D(W),D(L),D(L_0)$ for termwise derived exact functors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Assume $D(W)RR$, with the localized right-derived comparison unit, is a right derived functor of $WR$. For a complex $P$ of $\mathcal A$, write $\gamma_P:Q_{\mathcal B}C(R)P\to RR(Q_{\mathcal A}P)$ for the right-derived comparison unit and $\gamma^0$ for the corresponding unit of $RR_0$; $C(F)$ means applying an additive functor $F$ termwise. Let $b:D(W)RR\to RR_0D(V)$ be the canonical right-derived comparison, characterized by
$$b_{Q_{\mathcal A}P}D(W)(\gamma_P)=\gamma^0_{C(V)P}\,Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(c)_P),$$
using the canonical exact-functor localization identifications on both sides; let $a^D:D(V)D(L)\cong D(L_0)D(W)$ be induced termwise by $a$. Then for every $M\in D(\mathcal B)$, $N\in D(\mathcal A)$ and $t:D(L)M\to N$, the adjunct of $D(V)(t)(a^D_M)^{-1}$ is $b_ND(W)(t^\sharp)$. Equivalently, with $\eta,\varepsilon$ and $\eta_0,\varepsilon_0$ the two derived units and counits, one has
$$b_{D(L)M}D(W)(\eta_M)=RR_0(a^D_M)^{-1}\eta_{0,D(W)M},$$
$$D(V)(\varepsilon_N)=\varepsilon_{0,D(V)N}D(L_0)(b_N)a^D_{RRN}.$$
No invertibility of $b$, preservation of K-injectives by $V$, or geometric square is asserted.

proof.text:
Write $u,u_0$ for the underived units, to distinguish them from $\eta,\eta_0$. Exactness of $L,L_0$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify their left derived functors, including the comparison maps, with $D(L),D(L_0)$. For a complex $X$, naturality of $u$ with respect to each differential gives $R(L(d_X^i))u_{X^i}=u_{X^{i+1}}d_X^i$, so $C(u)_X$ is a chain map. Additive functors preserve the equation defining a chain homotopy, so these maps and the termwise adjunction descend to the homotopy categories used in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. In its canonical Hom formula, take $K=C(L)X$, $M=X$, both quasi-isomorphisms $s,t$ to be identities, and $f=C(u)_X:X\to C(R)C(L)X$. The representing right-derived cocone at the identity is $\gamma_{C(L)X}$; the left-derived cone at the identity is the exact localization identification. The underived adjunct of $f$ is $1_{C(L)X}$ (the triangle identity, degree by degree). Thus the inverse of the canonical Hom bijection sends $1_{D(L)Q_{\mathcal B}X}$ to $\gamma_{C(L)X}Q_{\mathcal B}(C(u)_X)$. By the definition of the unit of an adjunction this proves
$$\eta_{Q_{\mathcal B}X}=\gamma_{C(L)X}Q_{\mathcal B}(C(u)_X).$$
The same substitution for $L_0\dashv R_0$ gives $\eta_{0,Q_{\mathcal B_0}Y}=\gamma^0_{C(L_0)Y}Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(u_0)_Y)$. All formulas use the exact-functor localization identifications fixed in the statement.

proof.text:
Apply the stipulated underived adjunct compatibility to $t=1_{LM}$. Since its adjunct is $u_M$, and the adjunct under $L_0\dashv R_0$ of $a_M^{-1}:L_0WM\to VLM$ is $R_0(a_M^{-1})u_{0,WM}$, it gives $c_{LM}W(u_M)=R_0(a_M^{-1})u_{0,WM}$. Apply this equality in every degree of a complex $X$ of $\mathcal B$ and localize. Using Step 1 and the defining equation for $b$ at $P=C(L)X$, the left side of the desired derived-unit equation is
$$b_{D(L)QX}D(W)(\eta_{QX})=\gamma^0_{C(V)C(L)X}Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(c)_{C(L)X})Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(W)C(u)_X)$$
$$=\gamma^0_{C(V)C(L)X}Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(R_0)(C(a)_X^{-1}))Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(u_0)_{C(W)X})$$
$$=RR_0(Q_{\mathcal A_0}(C(a)_X^{-1}))\gamma^0_{C(L_0)C(W)X}Q_{\mathcal B_0}(C(u_0)_{C(W)X})$$
$$=RR_0((a^D_{QX})^{-1})\eta_{0,D(W)QX}.$$
Here $Q=Q_{\mathcal B}$ in subscripts. The third equality is precisely naturality of $\gamma^0$ for the complex isomorphism $C(a)_X^{-1}:C(L_0)C(W)X\to C(V)C(L)X$, and the last equality is Step 1 for $Y=C(W)X$. This is an equality of composites, not cancellation of $\gamma$ or an assumption that it is invertible.

proof.text: Both expressions $M\mapsto b_{D(L)M}D(W)(\eta_M)$ and $M\mapsto RR_0((a^D_M)^{-1})\eta_{0,D(W)M}$ are natural transformations from $D(W)$ to $RR_0D(V)D(L)$, by naturality of the displayed units, $a^D$ and $b$. Step 2 says their restrictions along the localization $Q_{\mathcal B}$ agree. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore makes them equal on $D(\mathcal B)$. This proves the asserted derived-unit identity for every $M$.

proof.text:
For $t:D(L)M\to N$, the adjunctions of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] give $t^\sharp=RR(t)\eta_M$. The adjunct under the second adjunction of $D(V)(t)(a^D_M)^{-1}$ is consequently
$$RR_0(D(V)(t))RR_0((a^D_M)^{-1})\eta_{0,D(W)M}
=RR_0(D(V)(t))b_{D(L)M}D(W)(\eta_M)
=b_ND(W)(RR(t))D(W)(\eta_M)=b_ND(W)(t^\sharp).$$
The first equality uses Step 3, and the second uses naturality of $b$ for $t$. The adjunct formula itself follows from the definition of the unit and functoriality of the Hom bijection.

proof.text:
Take $M=RRN$ and $t=\varepsilon_N$ in Step 4. The triangle identity gives $t^\sharp=1_{RRN}$, so the adjunct of $D(V)(\varepsilon_N)(a^D_{RRN})^{-1}$ is $b_N$. Applying the inverse Hom bijection, which sends $h$ to $\varepsilon_{0,D(V)N}D(L_0)(h)$, and composing on the right with $a^D_{RRN}$ yields
$$D(V)(\varepsilon_N)=\varepsilon_{0,D(V)N}D(L_0)(b_N)a^D_{RRN}.$$
Conversely the adjunct statement specialized to $t=1_{D(L)M}$ gives the unit equation; hence the displayed formulations are equivalent, as claimed.

tool_uses.why: Its exact-functor clause identifies the left derived functors and comparison maps without resolutions; no node of the Kunneth unit states this generic localization fact.
Its explicit identity-fraction Hom formula determines each derived unit from the underived unit; the Kunneth unit contains no such generic Hom formula.
Clause (3) extends an equality of natural transformations checked on complexes to the derived category; this generic localization uniqueness is not a Kunneth-unit theorem.
Its canonical functorial Hom bijection supplies the two derived adjunctions; this is a categorical tool underlying the coefficient-forgetting comparison, not a replacement of the Kunneth proof route.
